web_title: 5. Leading KPIs, Capacity Runway & Management Walk-the-Talk Audit
book_title: Chapter 5: The Operator's Scorecard — KPIs, Capacity & Walk-the-Talk
question: Which 6 leading operational KPIs govern Yash's trajectory, how large is its capacity runway, and has Keyur Shah's management team delivered on past promises?

epigraph.quote: Measure management not by the ambition of its slide deck, but by the gap between last year's timeline and this year's factory floor.
epigraph.author: Governance Underwriting Standard

web_blocks.title: 5.1 Six Leading Operational KPIs to Track

web_blocks.html: Condenser bushings carry 15-to-20-month delivery cycles and multi-year utility approvals. Financial statements therefore lag operational reality. The six leading KPIs below track Yash Highvoltage's real-time momentum:

web_blocks.caption: Yash Highvoltage Leading Operational KPI Dashboard
rows: Provides 15–20 months revenue visibility; watch quarterly book-to-bill >1.0x [1][2].
+40% YoY volume growth in H1 FY27; validates real demand beyond pricing [1].
Halol + Jarod combined capacity doubles unit headroom [1].
Higher RIP mix drives structural gross margin expansion (48.3% in H1 FY27) [1].
Diversifies away from domestic OEM cyclicality; US 27-state push [1][5].
Must stay <75 days as scale doubles; watch receivable days (66d in Sep-26) [2].
web_blocks.takeaway: Every leading indicator moved favorably in H1 FY27, with order book doubling in six months to ₹760 Cr and CCC compressing 18 days to 63 days [1][2].

web_blocks.title: 5.2 Capacity Expansion, Backward Integration & TAM Runway

web_blocks.html: Yash is building a ₹220 crore greenfield RIP/RIS plant at Jarod, Vadodara (2.5 lakh sq. ft. land; 1.5 lakh sq. ft. built-up) [1][2]. By September 30, 2026, it had spent ₹106 crore, with ₹114 crore slated over the next 12 months [1][2]. Combined capacity across Halol (Unit-1) and Jarod (Unit-2) reaches 15,000 units by end-CY26, adding ~6,000 RIP/RIS units yearly [1]. Phase 1 assembly using imported cores issued its first Jarod invoice on 30 September 2026 [1]. The IMPL winding machine is running, and the Menzel line is commissioning for Q3 FY27 [1]. On 23 November 2026, Yash invited analysts and institutional investors to a physical plant visit on 27 November 2026 [35].

In August 2026 (approved June 2026), Yash raised ₹151 crore via equity (₹91 Cr, 12.6 lakh shares) and convertible warrants (₹60 Cr, 8.3 lakh warrants, 25% paid upfront) [1]. Those funds back Phase 2 indigenous RIP/RIS cores up to 550 kV (₹80 Cr capex, ₹36.75 Cr working capital, ₹30 Cr GCP) [1]. On 14 November 2026, Monitoring Agency Acuité Ratings & Research Limited filed its Q2 FY27 report confirming zero deviation in preferential-issue proceeds utilization [33]. Management guides for 3x–4x revenue potential over five years at full scale (₹900–1,000 crore across Halol and Jarod by FY31), backed by a ₹760+ crore backlog and 27-state US sales coverage [1][5]. However, Indian Ministry of Power PLI incentives for RIP bushings remain unsecured.

An objective audit of Chairman & MD Keyur Shah and Executive Director (Finance) Darshan Thakkar shows strong commercial execution. It also highlights specific timeline slips, guidance ambiguities, and control gaps that require monitoring:

Launched 245 kV RIP (2020) & OIP (2022); RIP now 86% of revenue [1].
US IEEE market entry & seismic qualification
Yash HV USA Inc. live; 27 US states covered; 138/230 kV IEEE seismic passed; export orders still 5–7% of backlog (~₹40–50 Cr) [1][5].
Swung from ₹2.19 Cr FY26 loss to ₹55 lakh PAT in H1 FY27 within 9 months; targets ₹150–160 Cr sales in 4–5 years [1][2].
Originally targeted March 2026 trials; imported-core assembly billed 30 Sep 2026 (~6-mo slip); full indigenous core production slated Q3/H2 FY27 ahead of mid-2027 Swiss supply sunset [1][3].
Acuité Nov 14 report confirmed zero deviation on ₹151 Cr pref proceeds & H1 FY27 CFO hit ₹45.2 Cr, but FY26 saw ₹2.10 Cr vendor-email cyber fraud and DSO rose to 66 days [1].
web_blocks.takeaway: Management has delivered on technical qualifications, US network setup, Sukrut turnaround, and zero-deviation capex deployment; key execution tests are Q3/H2 FY27 indigenous RIP core production before mid-2027 and sustained DSO/internal-control discipline.

web_blocks.title: Verbatim Management Commentary — H1 FY27 Earnings Call (Oct 21, 2026; BSE Filing Oct 26, 2026)
paragraphs: Yash Highvoltage does not list a separate Chief Financial Officer on the call; Chairman & MD Keyur Shah leads operations while Executive Director (Finance) Darshan Thakkar leads financial commentary [2].

Keyur Shah (Chairman & MD) on margin discipline & core localization: “Honestly, sir, I would not want to make any tall commitments... sooner or later we will also be able to exactly know what sort of margin expansion come with the localized production. I would want to see and then make commitment.” He added on the 18%–20% duty-and-freight saving: “The cost saving, the import duty and the freight put together is today, say, 18% to 20%. That definitely goes away... But we have to also see how the customer is wanting us to give a price different than what it was they were giving for an imported core versus an Indian core, because the competition will also offer from India.” [2]

Darshan Thakkar (Executive Director, Finance) on H1 FY27 margins, backlog & working capital: “Gross margin for H1 FY27 was 48.3% compared with 42.4% in H1 of previous year. Product mix and operating leverage, which is a combination of volume increase of close to 40%, better price realization, and cost efficiency measures, were the main contributors... On the order book, as on 30th September 2026, our order book stands at INR 760 crores, up from INR 400 crores at the start of the financial year... The cash conversion cycle stands at 63 days as on 30th September '26 compared to 81 days for the full year ended FY26.” [2]

web_blocks.title: 5.4 Medium-Term TAM Runway & Order-Book Conversion Mechanics

web_blocks.html: India's transformer market should grow from $3.0 billion in 2025 to $4.47 billion by 2030, an 8.33% CAGR [1]. Meanwhile, US power transformer demand is up 119% since 2019, with 100 GW of new peak load needed by 2030 [1]. This addressable demand extends well past Yash's ₹389 crore annualized run-rate [1]. Its ₹760+ crore order book on September 30, 2026 nearly doubled from ₹400+ crore in March [1][2]. That backlog gives 15 to 20 months of visibility through 24–36 month blanket OEM orders with raw-material pass-through clauses [1][2]. Still, two disclosure nuances stand out. Both backlog figures are rounded floors rather than audited order ledgers. Management's FY27 revenue commentary also spans two unreconciled figures—40–45% growth (₹329–341 Cr) versus ₹360–400 Cr of invoicing (53–70% growth)—after H1 alone delivered ₹194.5 Cr.

Management guides for ~4x asset turnover on incremental greenfield capex once Jarod hits full utilization [1]. Yash has spent ₹106 crore of the ₹220 crore Jarod outlay, with ₹114 crore left over 12 months [1][2]. Acuité Ratings verified zero deviation on preferential proceeds through 30 September 2026 [33]. Yash has pre-funded the physical capacity for its 3x–4x five-year revenue goal [1][2]. Localized 420 kV and 550 kV lines target Q4 FY28 at the latest, with no major greenfield capex planned in FY28–FY29 [1][2].

The Sukrut Electric joint venture adds a second growth lever in Pune [1][2]. Yash and Quality Power acquired Sukrut 50:50 from Maschinenfabrik Reinhausen for ₹5.24 crore (Yash's share) [1][2]. Sukrut swung from a ₹2.19 crore FY26 loss to a ₹55 lakh profit in H1 FY27 [1][2][40]. Management aims to scale Sukrut from ~₹25–26 crore turnover to ₹150–160 crore over four to five years, adding complementary transformer-tank cross-sell.

book_paragraphs: When you and I track a fast-growing industrial company, reported earnings tell us what happened twelve months ago. To know where the business is heading twelve months from now, we need a dashboard of leading operational indicators.

At Yash Highvoltage, six numbers tell the whole story. First, the order book: it stood at ₹150 crore in March 2025, climbed to ₹400+ crore in March 2026, and surged to ₹760+ crore by September 2026—giving fifteen to twenty months of execution visibility, even after noting that management reports backlog as rounded floors and has cited two unreconciled FY27 revenue ranges (40–45% growth versus ₹360–400 crore invoicing). Second, physical volume: Yash sold 7,272 bushings in FY26 and roughly 4,000 units in just the first half of FY27, a 40% year-on-year volume jump. This is not merely price inflation; more bushings are leaving the factory floor.

Third and fourth are mix shifts: RIP bushings sit at 86% of product revenue (on ~40% of unit volume), while Exports plus Repair & Services climbed from 9% to 14% of channel revenue in H1 FY27. Fifth is installed capacity, which is doubling from roughly 7,000–10,000 units to 15,000 units across Halol and Jarod—with Acuité Ratings' 14 November 2026 Monitoring Agency Report confirming zero deviation in preferential-issue deployment and management opening the plant to institutional visitors on 27 November 2026. Sixth is the cash conversion cycle, which tightened from 81 days in FY26 to 63 days in H1 FY27.

book_subsections.title: Grading Keyur Shah's Walk-the-Talk Record
paragraphs: How has management's execution measured up against its promises? Honestly, the commercial scorecard is strong, with three concrete caveats worth watching. Keyur Shah promised to climb the voltage curve to 245 kV, break into the US IEEE market, turn around the Pune-based Sukrut Electric joint venture, and deploy expansion funds cleanly. Every one of those happened: Yash passed seismic qualification on 138 kV and 230 kV IEEE bushings, signed representation across 27 US states, swung Sukrut from a ₹2.19 crore loss to a ₹55 lakh profit in nine months, and earned a zero-deviation Monitoring Agency Report from Acuité Ratings on 14 November 2026.

Where should you keep a skeptical eye? First, Jarod's trial timeline slipped roughly six months from early post-IPO expectations of March 2026: imported-core assembly billed its first invoice on 30 September 2026, leaving full end-to-end indigenous RIP core manufacturing pending Q3/H2 FY27 against a hard mid-2027 sunset on Swiss partner core supply. Second, exports are still only 6% of revenue (5–7% of the backlog), and US tariff headwinds plus unapproved Indian PLI incentives raise the bar on FY28 export conversion. Third, an operational lapse in March 2026—a ₹2.10 crore vendor-email cyber fraud—showed internal payment controls had to catch up with rapid scale.

callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
callouts.text: Notice Keyur Shah's restraint on the H1 FY27 call: when an analyst pushed him to guide for 35% EBITDA margins after core integration, he declined to make tall commitments. Under-promising on margins while delivering 28.1% is healthy—provided indigenous RIP cores hit commercial production on schedule before mid-2027.

book_subsections.title: What to Watch Quarter by Quarter Over the Next 18 Months
paragraphs: If you are tracking Yash Highvoltage over FY27 and FY28, your checklist is remarkably concrete. First, watch for formal confirmation—starting with takeaways from the 27 November 2026 physical plant visit—that end-to-end indigenous RIP/RIS core winding and impregnation at Jarod has moved from prototype trials into full commercial production during Q3/H2 FY27 well ahead of MGC Moser Glaser's mid-2027 core-supply sunset. That single milestone enables both lower unit costs and RIP export eligibility.

Second, watch the order book and quarterly book-to-bill ratio. At ₹760+ crore in September 2026, Yash has more than 1.9x its annualized H1 revenue sitting in backlog; sustaining healthy order inflows while converting export homologation into firm orders beyond the current ~₹40–50 crore export backlog will confirm that the US 27-state network can overcome November 2026 Section 301 tariff proposals.

Third, watch receivable days, supplier advances, and inventory turns. Management brought the cash conversion cycle down to 63 days in H1 FY27 even as revenue nearly doubled, partly aided by higher payables and customer advances. Keeping CCC below 70 days as Jarod ramps and receivable days (66 days in Sep-26) normalize will prove that growth is durably self-funding.
